title: MicroRNA classifiers show weak separation of sepsis from non-infectious inflammation
summary: In 299 public whole-blood samples, learned classifiers evaluated literature-curated microRNAs for sepsis discrimination. The selected miR-150-5p/miR-486-5p pair had ROC-AUC 0.95 against healthy controls and 0.64 against non-infectious inflammation; adding the second marker gave no significant improvement. This is retrospective, cross-validated evidence from one cohort. Healthy controls differed demographically; an interstitial-fluid device was proposed but not built or validated.
ai_technology: Standardized logistic-regression screening; SVM, multilayer perceptron, random forest and XGBoost evaluation
organization: University of Patras; Hellenic Pasteur Institute; Vin University; United Arab Emirates University

evidence.tested: 158 sepsis cases, 82 healthy controls and 59 non-infectious inflammation controls; 263 candidate miRNAs. The paired marker gave nested-CV pooled AUC 0.83 (95% CI 0.78–0.88), with no independent cohort. Against non-infectious controls, no tested panel exceeded 0.64.
evidence.unknown: Clinical utility, prospective performance and interstitial-fluid transfer are unestablished. Whole-blood cell composition and unmeasured clinical covariates may confound associations; no causal role is established.
evidence.ai_role: Fixed logistic regression screened literature-curated single miRNAs and pairs under 10-fold cross-validation; further classifier families were compared under 5-fold cross-validation.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced publisher JATS abstract, exhaustive miRNA screening, classifier comparison and limitations, plus affiliations and publication metadata. The represented result is retrospective host-biomarker discrimination; the proposed device and preliminary bench proof are not treated as clinical or AI validation.
